scope: 108 bounded synthetic native MLX affine dequantization/forward/transpose/input-only VJP cases. This review authorizes interpretation only within this small component scope, not checkpoint or model support.

findings.detail: Original (y,), (dx,) unpacking treated a single-array VJP output as a singleton sequence: batch1 could lose its batch axis and batch3 could raise. Current y, (dx,) preserves output; exact shape guards reject broadcasting.

Original BF16 atol .03 alone accepted zero forward outputs for three actual batch1/group32 fixtures. Current elementwise AND relative-L2 gates reject all actual nonzero fixture outputs replaced by zero or sign reversal. Decode separately requires exact dtype-rounded values.

reviewed_contract.frozen_primal_scope: Only input tensor is a vjp primal; packed weights and affine metadata are closed-over constants. The reference derivative is dy @ W.
reviewed_contract.comparison: Decode exact dtype-rounded values (including host BF16 RN-even); matrix/gradient both elementwise and relative-L2 thresholds declared before native execution.

dispatch_requirements: Recheck every bound implementation/environment/library file before and after execution. Use the explicitly pinned affine-env interpreter.
Use a new receipt path and retain any failed attempt; exit0 requires every case and every comparison to pass.
Use an external short timeout; this tiny one-process harness has no internal deadline.
limitations: The fixture uses dyadic exactly representable metadata/input/cotangent values; it tests packing, signed/zero scales, group boundaries and quantized multiplication, not arbitrary metadata quantization error.
Output rows32 and batch1/3 exercise small GEMV-like shapes only. No large GEMM, long-context shapes, broadcast, partial group or checkpoint tensors are qualified.
The explicit transpose and input VJP may dispatch the same MLX primitive; each is independently checked against binary64 reference math, but they are not independent native engines.
The host round-to-dtype projection calculation reported here is a CPU sanity bound, not a prediction or measurement of device error.
Finite per-fixture tolerances do not certify all elementwise gradient signs near zero or arbitrary model gradient correctness.
No adapter optimizer, model, external ngram table, EXL3 trellis, QSA/GDN composition or training qualification.
Read-through .pth isolates process configuration but reuses the existing native MLX distribution; it is not an independently built implementation.
This review does not qualify GPU results until a successful receipt on the bound runtime is inspected.
